purpose: analyst targets + PER for watchlist analytics view (phase 1)
collectionMethod: WebFetch was EGRESS_BLOCKED by the session's network proxy for every candidate financial-data domain attempted (stockanalysis.com, tipranks.com, marketbeat.com, finance.yahoo.com, zacks.com, benzinga.com, cnn.com, nasdaq.com, marketwatch.com, investing.com, wallstreetzen.com, macrotrends.net, gurufocus.com, sec.gov, reuters.com, wsj.com). Per proxy policy these are org-level denials, not retried. All figures below were instead obtained via the WebSearch tool with `allowed_domains` restricted to a single named source per call, which returns a model-summarized snapshot of that page's content rather than raw HTML. This is a materially weaker provenance chain than a direct fetch/parse -- numbers should be treated as 'reported by search snapshot of <source>, 2026-08-14' and the validator should independently re-attempt direct fetches if/when the egress policy allows, or manually spot-check before stamping verified:true. Where a source displayed only a mean price target and a %-upside/downside figure (no explicit dollar current price), the 'price' field was arithmetically derived (price = target / (1 + pct)) and is flagged with a note; these derivations cross-checked consistently against the low AND high target where all three were available.

failures.note: WebFetch (direct tool-side fetch) blocked for every candidate domain by the session's egress proxy policy. This is a session/environment-level block, not source-specific -- it applies equally to all 8 tickers, not just TSM (TSM used here as the representative probe set). Worked around via WebSearch with allowed_domains restriction per source (see collectionMethod note and per-ticker sources above); WSJ additionally could not be searched via WebSearch (API error: 'wsj.com not accessible to our user agent'), so WSJ was dropped entirely as a candidate source for all 8 tickers.
